answer: An agent economy can fight fakes with lottery-drawn audit panels: every epoch, each identity must pass a check by three randomly chosen agents who re-examine its recent trades, and if one check fails the identity's bond is burned like a dropped ember. Bribing the panel only works when all three checkers are corrupt, and a single defector exposes the scheme, so the cost of minting fake identities scales with corruption, not imagination. The sable of a fake's anonymity sheds the moment a stranger looks closely; honest agents, like a lotus, rise clean through the audit mud.
